subject: Maths
subtopic: Representing inequalities on a number line
title: Representing inequalities on a number line
subtitle: Linear Inequalities · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can represent linear inequalities on a number line using open and closed circles.

key_vocab.definition: On a number line, an open circle (○) means the value is NOT included (). A closed circle (●) means the value IS included (≤ or ≥).

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can represent linear inequalities on a number line using open and closed circles.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: open circle -- On a number line, an open circle (○) means the value is NOT included (). A closed circle (●) means the value IS included (≤ or ≥).

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Open circle = not included (strict). Closed circle = included (or equal to). Arrow shows the direction of valid values.
○ for ; ● for ≤ ≥
Open = excluded, Closed = included

Key examples:
  ✓ x > 3: open circle at 3, arrow right  (not including 3)
  ✓ x ≤ 5: closed circle at 5, arrow left  (including 5)
  ✓ 2 < x ≤ 6: open at 2, closed at 6, line between  (compound)
  ✗ x > 3 uses a closed circle at 3  (strict means open)
  ✗ x ≤ 5 means arrow pointing right from 5  (less than means left)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – simple inequality
  Represent x > 2 on a number line
  Draw a number line with 2 marked
  Place an open circle at 2 (not included)
  Draw an arrow pointing right from 2
  Open circle at 2, arrow right
  (The open circle shows that 2 itself is not a solution.)

Example 2 – less than or equal
  Represent x ≤ 4 on a number line
  Draw a number line with 4 marked
  Place a closed circle at 4 (included)
  Draw an arrow pointing left from 4
  Closed circle at 4, arrow left
  (The closed circle shows that 4 IS a solution.)

sections.title: Drawing simple inequalities
sections.content:
Describe the number line representation.

(a) x > 5
(b) x ≤ 2
(c) x ≥ −3
(d) x < 0

sections.title: Reading number lines
sections.content:
Write the inequality shown.

(a) Closed circle at 4, arrow right
(b) Open circle at −2, arrow left
(c) Open at 1, closed at 5, line between
(d) Closed at −3, open at 2, line between

sections.title: Compound inequalities
sections.content:
Describe the number line for each compound inequality.

(a) 1 < x < 4
(b) −2 ≤ x ≤ 3
(c) 0 < x ≤ 5
(d) −4 ≤ x < −1

sections.title: Solve then represent
sections.content:
Solve the inequality, then describe the number line.

(a) 3x > 12
(b) x + 5 ≤ 8
(c) 2x − 1 ≥ 5
(d) 4x + 3 < 15

sections.title: Mixed problems
sections.content:
Solve and represent on a number line.

(a) 5 ≤ 2x + 1 < 11
(b) −3 < x + 2 ≤ 4
(c) x ≥ −1 and x < 4
(d) 3x − 2 > 1 and 2x < 10
(e) −4 ≤ 3x + 2 ≤ 11

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ An open circle means the value is NOT included
✗ x > 3 uses a closed circle at 3
✓ x ≤ 5 means closed circle at 5 with arrow pointing left
✗ For x < 4, the arrow points right from 4
✓ A compound inequality has two endpoints and a line between them

teacher_sections.title: Teacher Key & Mark Scheme
teacher_sections.content:
Award marks for correct working and final answers.

Drawing simple inequalities:
  (a) Open circle at 5, arrow right
  (b) Closed circle at 2, arrow left
  (c) Closed circle at −3, arrow right
  (d) Open circle at 0, arrow left

Reading number lines:
  (a) x ≥ 4
  (b) x < −2
  (c) 1 < x ≤ 5
  (d) −3 ≤ x < 2

Compound inequalities:
  (a) Open at 1, open at 4, line between
  (b) Closed at −2, closed at 3, line between
  (c) Open at 0, closed at 5, line between
  (d) Closed at −4, open at −1, line between

Solve then represent:
  (a) x > 4: open at 4, arrow right
  (b) x ≤ 3: closed at 3, arrow left
  (c) x ≥ 3: closed at 3, arrow right
  (d) x < 3: open at 3, arrow left

Mixed problems:
  (a) 2 ≤ x < 5: closed at 2, open at 5
  (b) −5 < x ≤ 2: open at −5, closed at 2
  (c) Closed at −1, open at 4, line between
  (d) 1 < x < 5: open at 1, open at 5
  (e) −2 ≤ x ≤ 3: closed at −2, closed at 3
